claims.statement: Nearly all oxyromon tests are unit tests of the binary crate: they live in src/<module>/test_*.rs, are pulled in by `#[cfg(test)] mod test_name;` at the bottom of the parent module, and reach the code under test via `use super::*`, so they can call a subcommand's `main()` directly with a synthesized clap ArgMatches without spawning a process. tests/ holds only two test targets (crates.rs, mcp_stdio.rs); mcp_stdio.rs is the sole suite that spawns the real binary via CARGO_BIN_EXE_oxyromon.

The canonical test skeleton is: acquire the global MUTEX, build a DB from a NamedTempFile via establish_connection, create ROM and TMP directories with TempDir::new_in("tests") and point the settings at them, import a DAT through import_dats::subcommand()/main(), then act and assert; a ProgressBar::hidden() stands in for the real bar so the production print_* helpers still run.

establish_connection() is the single DB entry point used by both main.rs and the tests: it runs the embedded MIGRATOR and the full PRAGMA block, and its pool geometry is compile-time feature dependent — 5 connections with NORMAL locking under `server` or `mcp`, 1 connection with EXCLUSIVE otherwise — so the same test source exercises two different database configurations depending on the feature flags.

Scratch directories are created with TempDir::new_in("tests") rather than in /tmp so fixtures and their imported results stay on one filesystem — exercising rename_file's rename path instead of its cross-device copy+delete fallback — and their leftovers are covered by the `tests/.tmp*` gitignore entry.

set_rom_directory and set_tmp_directory exist only under cfg(test), in the same cfg_if! block in config.rs as MUTEX; production code has no equivalent and instead goes through get_rom_directory/get_tmp_directory, which fall back to OXYROMON_ROM_DIRECTORY, $HOME/Emulation and env::temp_dir() and persist the value. Because the settings live in the per-test DB, no test sets or unsets environment variables.

The global `MUTEX` is a cfg(test)-only `LazyLock<tokio::sync::Mutex<i32>>` in config.rs taken as the first statement of a test; because all ~300 in-crate test modules compile into one binary, holding it makes that suite effectively sequential, which is the price for the process-wide state they share (the global MULTI_PROGRESS, the tests/ directory hosting every scratch dir, and fixed loopback ports).

The MUTEX is deliberately not universal: pure #[test] units (mimetype matchers, crc32, GraphQL validators, compute_alpha_subfolder, prompt_for_games) and database-only tests that touch no shared directory, such as sort_roms/test_all_regions_from_matches.rs, acquire no guard.
AGENTS.md lists a forgotten test MUTEX under Common Pitfalls: the failure mode is flakiness in a full run rather than a deterministic error.

Where a suite factors the preamble into a setup() helper it must return the NamedTempFile and both TempDirs so the caller keeps them alive for the whole test; a dropped guard deletes the directory or database the pool and the assertions still point at.

Prompts must never block tests: prompt_for_games(games, all) returns the list untouched when `all` is true, and the two call sites pass cfg!(test) for exactly that reason, so the dialoguer multiselect is never constructed under test. A new interactive call site needs its own bypass or the suite hangs.
Import helpers take an explicit UnattendedMode { None, Skip, First } instead of relying on cfg!(test); tests pass UnattendedMode::Skip to avoid interactive selection.

Tool-dependent tests skip rather than fail: an availability probe using get_version() is the first statement of the test, before the mutex, and version floors such as chdman::MIN_SPLITBIN_VERSION ("0.265") return early when the installed version sorts lower. A skipped test is reported as passing, so a tool-gated path can be silently unexercised.

get_version() is the single definition of tool availability shared by product and test: the same functions feed the `info` dependency report and the GraphQL `dependencies` field, and CI installs only mame-tools (chdman) and xdelta3, so the other interop suites skip there by design.

Tests assert database rows and on-disk layout together: sort_roms/test_sort.rs checks each romfile.path equals the expected path relative to ROM_DIRECTORY and that rom_directory.join(path) is a file; purge_roms/test_orphans.rs asserts find_romfiles() is empty and the system directory has zero entries; check_roms/test_check_by_name.rs corrupts the imported file after import and asserts the row's path contains /Trash/ with the file present there.

DAT-download functions take the provider base URL as a parameter, so HTTP tests mount a wiremock MockServer and pass mock_server.uri() into the function under test — dependency injection, not an environment override. wiremock is the root package's only dev-dependency.

Server tests boot the real Axum main(pool, &matches) in one future and the reqwest client in another, racing them with tokio::select! after a fixed warm-up sleep (1000 ms in the first case, 100 ms elsewhere); multipart bodies are hand-assembled, background imports are awaited by sleeping then re-querying, and each test pins its own loopback port (default 8000, or 8001-8003 and 8010-8012) while holding the MUTEX.

server and mcp modules are feature-gated in main.rs, so `cargo test` without `--features oxyromon/server` compiles none of src/server/ or tests/mcp_stdio.rs and is vacuously green for that code; `server` implies `mcp`, so the single workspace command runs both.

The suite is run with `cargo test --workspace --features oxyromon/server` (the package-qualified feature is required because --workspace selects several packages), coverage with `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --features oxyromon/server --lcov --output-path lcov.info` as CI does, per-crate with `cargo test -p <crate>`, and slow tests with `-- --ignored`; only one workspace test is #[ignore]d, the 2 GiB index_shift_round_trips in crates/xso-rs.

test.sh runs the llvm-cov pass twice, and its second line selects oxyromon/nod and oxyromon/sevenz, which the root [features] table no longer declares (nod and sevenz-rust2 are plain dependencies); the pass adds no coverage and, writing to the same lcov.info, only overwrites the first run's report.

Debug-build test speed is dominated by dependencies: [profile.dev.package."*"] sets opt-level = 3 because hashing and the pure-Rust codecs run roughly an order of magnitude slower at opt-level 0, and wall-clock time for the in-crate suite scales with the number of serialized #[tokio::test] modules rather than CPU count.

tests/crates.rs is a workspace parity guard, not a behaviour test: it requires the five format-crate CLI ui.rs copies to be byte-identical, so editing one without the others turns any `cargo test --workspace` red.

A new subcommand is expected to ship tests in src/<command>/test_*.rs, one scenario per file named for the behaviour, each registered with #[cfg(test)] mod test_*; catalogue state is built by importing a DAT through import_dats::main rather than inserting rows, except for pure path-building helpers such as common/test_path_*.rs which construct System/Game/Rom structs in place.
